restrictions: Applies only to poseidon-orchard-r10-prefix-v1 and the line construction defined in proof.md sections 2-4; no claim is made for another round count.

Worst-case work is N_max=8669211530023973, derived by the embedded exact-integer ledger. Stage B is 148386783813197, stage C is 5937454131022267, and stage D is 2583370481286514; no predecessor total is an input.

The footprint is 9895806318240 bytes: arena 9895805916160, code/static 356352, register file 12384, offline workspace 576, and stack 32768. Section 7 lists every allocation, slab class, and call-chain frame.

Machine restriction: one 387-word file (256 field and 131 integer words); running-twiddle product passes through seven layers, eight-position column loops, four-block bodies and twiddle-one group-zero variants. No product twiddle table in C or D.
Stage D charges the normal sequence with quotient and return tests and ABORTs at the first failure after a charged prefix. H-NORMAL affects success probability only, not the time or memory bound.

success_probability is over the fresh words of section 4.1.1. Stage C zero-tests each batch prefix and ABORTs on a zero; delta_C <= 4.07505558544531428109415424692223780742399603466636571890512060525331371214257371598410062E-55. Section 9.2 substitutes q=0.3931, delta=0.001, eps_iso=2^-48, eps_coin<2^-122, and this delta_C.

heuristics.statement: Let p=28948022309329048855892746252171976963363056481941560715954676764349967630337 be the Pallas prime, F the fixed poseidon-orchard-r10-prefix-v1 line polynomial of degree D=152587890625, and g_c the monic odd part of F about a centre c. Let k(c) count the usable nonzero-square roots of g_c, equivalently the degree event entering Stage D. For c uniform on F_p, at least 0.3931 p centres have 1 <= k(c) <= 16. The success bound is 0.39209 and subtracts the proved Stage-C term delta_C<=4.07505558544531428109415424692223780742399603466636571890512060525331371214257371598410062E-55.
heuristics.scope: The fixed Poseidon target poseidon-orchard-r10-prefix-v1, this line construction (the line j = 0 of the first two rounds, odd part about a centre, proof.md sections 2-3), the polynomial F of proof.md section 2.3; centres uniform on F_p. Not claimed for other round counts. The other terms of the success bound are H-NORMAL (proof.md 9.5) and proved terms: the coin bias, the stage-C zero test and the isolation lemma (proof.md 4.1.1, 9.2, 9.4); the time and memory bounds do not depend on the premise.
heuristics.extrapolation: Proof section 9.3 contains the signed-permutation moments, the 27-case toy-field table and the explicit extrapolation to depth 16. Proof section 10.3 contains the exact cycle types, specialization centres, lifted sign-kernel witnesses and deployed-constant computations through three layers.
heuristics.limitations: It concerns this F, not every polynomial of degree D: it is false for permutation polynomials (k = 0 at every centre) and for a decomposable F with imprimitive monodromy (the axis line of proof.md 10.3, Theorem C), and false at one layer (m = 2: the law gives exactly 0.375). At N = 16 neither the monodromy nor the counts are computed (Weil's bound exceeds p for the fibre powers of degree 5^16); the premise is the extrapolation of a law that is a theorem at N = 2, 3 and measured on toy fields and at N <= 5. The organizer tests compute k(c) inside the submitted program; the runner checks only the returned witness pairs, so they are evidence under trusted execution of that program, printed in full in experiments/exp_euclid.py. The success bound assumes nothing about the organizer-seeded trials (no independence or identical distribution of the trials is used).

heuristics.statement: For the centre c uniform on F_p, the Euclidean remainder sequence of (g_c, R_c - 1), where g_c is the monic odd part of proof.md section 3 (degree m = 76,293,945,312) and R_c = S^((p-1)/2) mod g_c, is normal down to its gcd (deg(R_c - 1) = m - 1 and every quotient has degree 1) except with probability at most delta = 0.001 (2^-9.966). Stage D is charged for the normal sequence; every division tests its quotient degree and every call of the half-gcd its return, and on any other case the trial ends (ABORT, proof.md 4.4, 6.3). With H-ONE (q = 0.3931) and one centre (K = 1) the success bound is q - delta - delta_C - eps_coin - eps_iso = 0.39209 (proof.md 9.2). The combined lower bound is conservatively reported as 0.39209 and subtracts delta_C<=4.07505558544531428109415424692223780742399603466636571890512060525331371214257371598410062E-55.
heuristics.scope: The pairs (g_c, R_c - 1) of the target poseidon-orchard-r10-prefix-v1, c uniform on F_p. It enters only the success probability: the time and memory bounds hold for every remainder sequence, because a trial with an abnormal sequence ends at its first failed test after executing a prefix of the charged work (proof.md 6.3). Not claimed for other round counts. The premise is bradcush's (entries e6dcb600 and 1aa56884); the organizer-run tests follow gta6rp's entries (fe269c23); the split of the success allowance (q = 0.3931 with a separate H-NORMAL delta, here 0.001) follows cryptogakusei's entry 4888e783; delta = 0.001 is that of our accepted r = 9 entry 5b96dbb5.
heuristics.extrapolation: For a uniformly random pair of degrees m and m - 1 the sequence is abnormal exactly when one of the m principal subresultant coefficients vanishes, each a nonzero polynomial of degree at most 2m in the coefficients, so by Schwartz-Zippel the probability is at most 2 m^2 / p < 2^-180.7; the premise extrapolates a much weaker form of this random-pair behaviour (delta = 0.001) to the structured pair (g_c, R_c - 1). Measured support, organizer-run (proof.md 10.5.1): the six experiments euclid-normal-n2-t256-l2-a to -f compute the complete Euclidean sequence of (g_c, R_c - 1) for this construction on the truncation F_2 of the digest polynomial (proof.md 10.3; m = 12) for 256 organizer-seeded trials of two centres each (3,072 sequences in all) and return a witness pair exactly when both sequences of a trial are normal; euclid-normal-n3-t24 and euclid-normal-n4-t2 do the same at m = 62, 312. Zero abnormal in the 3,072 sequences is a reproducible observation consistent with the premise; the organizer-seeded centres are not treated as independent unselected samples and no population bound is drawn from them (delta = 0.001 is the declared premise). Our local runs of the eight entries: 3,098 sequences, all normal. Reported by our earlier entries, not organizer-run (proof.md 10.5): the complete sequences on the sibling targets with r' = 0 (8 centres, m = 7,812) and r' = 1 (2 centres, m = 39,062), every quotient of degree 1.
heuristics.limitations: The Schwartz-Zippel bound does not transfer, because the coefficients of R_c have degree about p in those of g_c. The success bound stays at least 0.39 for every delta <= 0.0030999 (proof.md 9.2(d)), above the stated delta = 0.001. The organizer-run tests are at m = 12 to 312, far below m; normality is computed inside the submitted program and the runner checks only the returned witness pairs. The success bound assumes nothing about the organizer-seeded trials (no independence or identical distribution of the trials is used).
